_comment: HELD-OUT validation set for the M9 fusion-vs-vector-alone investigation
(see .genesis/checkpoints/CURRENT.md and PLAN.md's M9 entry for the
session that created this file). tests/fixtures/retrieval_queries.json
(the ORIGINAL 10) is used for ALL tuning/variant-selection; THIS file
is touched exactly once, after a single winning fusion variant has
already been chosen against the original 10 and frozen. The
methodological point: trying N fusion variants and keeping whichever
scores best on a small query set is fitting noise, not measuring
improvement -- this file exists so the chosen winner can be checked
against queries it was never tuned against, not selected among.
These 15 queries were written by reading backend/ source directly --
grepping for top-level def/class declarations not already used by the
original 10 (backend/memory/context_retriever.py::reciprocal_rank_fusion,
backend/webhook_receiver/validator.py::verify_signature,
backend/reliability/circuit_breaker.py::CircuitBreaker,
backend/webhook_receiver/parser.py::parse_pull_request_payload,
backend/agents/contracts.py::dedupe_findings,
backend/economics/budget.py::BudgetGuard,
backend/hitl/queue.py::route_review,
backend/economics/pricing.py::compute_cost_usd,
backend/memory/tiger_client.py::apply_migrations) -- and reading each
target's own docstring to write a faithful natural-language paraphrase
where the category calls for one. Chosen and committed BEFORE this
session ran hybrid_search against a single one of them: no query here
was picked, adjusted, or dropped because of how it scored. Coverage
mirrors the original set's mix (exact-identifier, natural-language,
and cases where a sibling chunk in the same file shares enough
vocabulary to make correct disambiguation a real test, mirroring the
original's id-6 BudgetGuard/BudgetExceededError pattern) rather than
reusing the same three category labels as decoration.
ids start at 11 (not 1) purely so a (query id) pair is never ambiguous
between the two files when both are referenced in the same report.
Same identity scheme as the original file: a target is (expected_path,
expected_symbol), not a row id, because ids are reassigned on every
TRUNCATE-and-reload re-seed.

queries.rationale: Literal class name, unique token in the corpus. (An earlier draft of this set used call_with_retry for ids 11/12, but that function's signature uses PEP 695 generic syntax -- def call_with_retry[T](... -- which _symbol_declaration_pattern's regex (\s*[(:] immediately after the name) cannot match through the [T]. Swapped to RetryPolicy, a plain dataclass declaration, before this file was committed or run against -- a fixture-authoring correctness fix, not a result-driven substitution.)

queries.query: tunable knobs for one retry loop: max attempts, backoff delay bounds, and jitter
queries.rationale: Same target as id 11, phrased as a natural-language paraphrase of RetryPolicy's own docstring ('Tunable knobs for one retry loop') instead of the identifier -- the exact-identifier/natural-language controlled-pair pattern the original set uses for ids 4/10, applied to a new target.
Literal class name, unique token in the corpus.

queries.query: lazily construct a shared background thread pool for running blocking calls under a timeout
queries.rationale: Paraphrase of _get_executor's own inline comment ('Lazily constructed ... guarded by a lock since multiple JobQueue instances ... may call run_with_timeout concurrently'), targeting a short private helper in the same file as ids 13/15 so all three compete for the same vocabulary.

queries.query: the exception raised when a wrapped call does not finish within its allotted time
queries.rationale: Paraphrase of CallTimedOutError's one-line docstring, deliberately in the same file as TimeoutPolicy and run_with_timeout (ids 13/14) which share heavy vocabulary overlap ('timeout', 'seconds', 'call', 'bounded') -- mirrors the original set's id-6 BudgetGuard/BudgetExceededError sibling-disambiguation pattern with a different file.
Literal function name, unique token in the corpus.

queries.query: record a completed LLM call's token counts and cost
queries.rationale: Paraphrase of emit_llm_call's own docstring ('Record a real LLM call's model/token/cost accounting') without the identifier. backend/observability/events.py defines several other emit_* functions (emit_tool_call, emit_decision, emit_span_start/end) sharing 'record'/'event'/'call' vocabulary, a genuine disambiguation test.
Literal class name, unique token in the corpus.

Literal class name, but a real stress test: 'webhook' is heavily repeated vocabulary across backend/webhook_receiver/{parser,router,validator}.py's docstrings and code, all of which are also indexed, so the exact model class (not the handling logic that talks about it) has real decoys to beat.

queries.query: parse a model's raw text response into validated findings, skipping any bad entries
queries.rationale: Paraphrase of parse_findings_from_llm_response's own docstring ('An individual item that fails Finding validation ... is logged and skipped rather than failing the whole batch') without the identifier.
Literal class name, unique token in the corpus.
Literal function name, unique token in the corpus.

queries.query: union two branches' error maps together in a shared graph state
queries.rationale: Paraphrase of _merge_dicts's own docstring ('Reducer for node_errors: union two branches' error maps') without the identifier. Targets a short, private (leading-underscore) helper function -- a real test of whether a short chunk with modest vocabulary overlap against the rest of backend/orchestrator/state.py's own GraphState-heavy docstring still surfaces.
Literal class/Protocol name, unique token in the corpus.
Literal function name; a FastAPI dependency-injection helper, structurally different code shape (short, decorator-adjacent) from most other targets in this set.
